book.title: The Telegraph All New Toughie Crossword, book 1

clue.text: This man Cromwell, not male well disposed to be one

definitions.text: This man Cromwell, not male well disposed to be one

indicators.note: to dispose things is to set them out in order, so these letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: 'not' tells us to strip the named pieces out of the surname, leaving only its first letters

parts.note: taken as written, before trimming
taken as written: the tail end of the surname

explanation.surface: A wry remark that Oliver Cromwell, the man who had a king executed, was hardly inclined to support the crown.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: Cromwell, who ran England as Lord Protector after Charles I was beheaded, was certainly no royalist.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter of rule by a king or queen, the very cause the regicide Cromwell fought against.

clue.text: Welsh town of an American character

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the county town of Flintshire in north Wales
second meaning: the US spelling of mould, a type or character, as in 'cast in the same mould'

explanation.walkthrough: Americans drop the U from mould, so the word for a person's type or character matches the Welsh town's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Mold is a Welsh market town, and in US spelling a mold is a kind or stamp of person.

clue.text: Maybe do something to explain text?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: do (doh) is one of the sol-fa syllables of the scale, and 'Maybe' marks it as an example
second meaning: a comment added to clarify a passage

explanation.walkthrough: 'do' looks like the verb but is the musical syllable.
explanation.definitionFit: Do is one example of a musical tone in sol-fa, and a footnote or annotation clarifies a text.

clue.text: French grocer set up without one method for handling food

indicators.note: in a down clue 'set up' means raised from bottom to top, so the word is read backwards
'without' says the following item is left out of the word

parts.note: épicier is French for grocer
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A French shopkeeper sets up shop lacking one way of dealing with food.
explanation.walkthrough: Of the two Is in the French word, dropping the second leaves the letters that read upwards as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of instructions for preparing a dish is a method for handling food.

clue.text: A man, Irish nut, and I am troubled by a principle of benevolence

indicators.note: something troubled is stirred up and disturbed, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two oddballs, a man and an eccentric Irishman, admit to being bothered by someone's kindly creed.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed copy is garbled by OCR; the anagram needs 'A man, Irish nut, and I am', which gives the fifteen letters exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: Humanitarianism is the doctrine of promoting human welfare, a creed founded on goodwill to others.

clue.text: Way little fellow goes round university town

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way

indicators.note: the short name wraps around the university letter, enclosing it

parts.note: Rod is a man's name cut short from Roderick, a fellow named in a little form

explanation.surface: A road where a small man walks around a college town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'university town' reads as one phrase, but the university is only the letter U and 'town' alone is the definition. STROUD is a market town in Gloucestershire.
explanation.definitionFit: Stroud is a market town in the Cotswolds of Gloucestershire, England.

clue.text: Declare nothing's been smuggled in a car

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: goods smuggled in a vehicle are hidden inside it, so the zero goes within the car

parts.note: VW, Volkswagen, is a make of car
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A traveller at customs insists that nothing has been hidden in the car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Declare' fits the customs scene, where it means listing goods; here it means state openly.
explanation.definitionFit: To avow is to state openly or affirm, a synonym of declare.

clue.text: Palace engendering excellent lines in poetry

indicators.note: the excellent lines are placed in the poetry, inside it

parts.note: verses are lines of poetry
A1 means first-rate; the 1 is read as the letter I
L is an abbreviation for line, so LL is lines

explanation.surface: A grand palace inspires superb poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engendering' only links the definition to the wordplay. A1, first-rate, often appears as AI in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Versailles is the vast royal palace built by Louis XIV outside Paris.

clue.text: Knowing about the East demanding to be put into a non-Eastern culture

indicators.note: the knowing word is wrapped about the other two pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: wise means knowing or shrewd
E is the abbreviation for East, and 'the' comes along with it
stern means strict and demanding

explanation.surface: An expert on the Orient insists on being absorbed into Western ways.
explanation.definitionFit: To westernise is to bring a person or place under the influence of the culture of Europe and America.

clue.text: 100 almost 'ere — unfortunately they may miss the boat

indicators.note: things that turn out unfortunately go wrong, so these letters fall into a different order

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
taken as written, not as an instruction to shorten anything
taken as written: the Cockney way of saying here

explanation.surface: A Cockney complains that a hundred people have nearly arrived, sadly too late for the ferry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' looks like an instruction to cut a letter off, but it is plain fodder for the anagram along with the dropped-H 'ere.
explanation.definitionFit: Latecomers arrive after the start, so they are the people liable to miss the boat, an idiom for missing an opportunity.

clue.text: A statistical value provided for the members

parts.note: taken as written
RMS, root mean square, is a statistical measure

explanation.surface: A figure from the statistics is supplied for the club's membership.
explanation.walkthrough: 'members' suggests club members but means limbs. RMS, root mean square, is a kind of average.
explanation.definitionFit: Members is an old word for limbs, and arms are limbs of the body.

clue.text: Time when a security person may be left in the dark

definitions.meaning: the answer names a period: a stint of guard duty through the dark hours

definitions.text: a security person may be left in the dark
definitions.meaning: a guard on the late shift is literally left alone in the dark, and the phrase also suggests being uninformed

explanation.walkthrough: 'left in the dark' looks like the idiom for being kept uninformed, but here it is literal: a guard on duty through the night.
explanation.definitionFit: A night watch is a period of guard duty kept through the hours of darkness.

clue.text: There's little right in bad manners and carelessness

indicators.note: the short right is put in, inside the bad manners

parts.note: impudence is cheeky rudeness
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Rudeness and carelessness leave little room for doing right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad manners and carelessness' looks like a list, but 'and' only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Imprudence is a lack of caution or good judgement, a failing close to rashness.

clue.text: Extend chute outside home

indicators.note: the chute is placed outside home, enclosing it

parts.note: a spout is a chute or pipe that liquid or grain pours down
in means at home

explanation.surface: An instruction to run a slide or pipe out from the house.
explanation.definitionFit: To spin out something is to prolong or stretch it, making it last longer.

clue.text: One who follows second person on the podium?

parts.note: a talker is a speaker, who stands on the podium to address an audience

explanation.surface: Someone who comes after the runner-up at a prizegiving.
explanation.walkthrough: The podium suggests a medal ceremony, with 'second person' the runner-up; it is the speaker's platform, and 'second' is just S.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalker pursues another person obsessively, so is literally one who follows.

clue.text: Historian understood America

parts.note: tacit means understood without being stated
US is short for the United States

explanation.surface: A scholar of the past who grasped what America was about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'understood' reads as a verb but supplies an adjective meaning implied.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacitus was a Roman historian, author of the Annals and the Histories.

clue.text: I'm locked up — I meant to reform

definitions.text: I'm locked up — I meant to reform

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to reform something is to form it again, so these letters are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A prisoner protests that they always intended to go straight.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: it is just what a prisoner might say. 'reform' suggests a convict's good intentions; here it signals rebuilding the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An inmate is a prisoner held in jail, someone who could truthfully say this.

clue.text: Loss of time after furious running around

indicators.note: the time piece comes after the reversed word
running around means turning back on itself, so the angry word is read backwards

parts.note: mad means furious
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Time wasted after a frantic dash about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loss of time' looks like the definition, but 'of' is only a link and 'Loss' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Damage is harm or loss suffered, as in damages paid to make up for it.

clue.text: Former political leader in ancient coat — there's bad, bad article about it

indicators.note: the first 'bad' goes about the ancient coat, wrapping round it

parts.note: harm, as in no bad will come of it
old means ancient
a mac is a raincoat, short for mackintosh
ill means bad
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A former statesman wears an old coat, prompting snide remarks about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The two 'bad's do different jobs: the first is a noun meaning harm, the second an adjective. Macmillan was British Conservative Prime Minister from 1957 to 1963.
explanation.definitionFit: Harold Macmillan was a British Prime Minister, leader of the Conservative Party until 1963.

clue.text: Theologian into marijuana with a partner

indicators.note: the theologian goes into the drug, inside it

parts.note: weed is slang for marijuana
DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a theology degree

explanation.surface: A divinity scholar who is keen on cannabis, smoking it with a companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' looks like 'keen on', but it is the instruction to put one piece inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: Wedded means married, joined to a spouse in matrimony.

clue.text: Particular parliament screening a film

indicators.note: screening means shielding, so the parliament holds the film within it

parts.note: the Dáil is the lower house of the Irish parliament
ET is Spielberg's film about an alien

explanation.surface: A specific assembly holds a showing of a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'screening' suggests showing a film; here it means hiding one inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A detail is a particular, an individual item or fact, as in going into particulars.

clue.text: Police officers may have suspicion about individual, not half!

indicators.note: the suspicion word goes about the trimmed individual, holding it

parts.note: sus is British slang for suspicion

indicators.note: only half of the word is kept, its first three letters

parts.note: a person is an individual

explanation.surface: Detectives might harbour a strong hunch about someone, and how!
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half!' is the British exclamation meaning very much, but here it cuts the word in half. Supers are superintendents, senior British police officers.
explanation.definitionFit: Super is short for superintendent, a senior rank of police officer in Britain.

clue.text: Fish brought aboard ship behaves like a whale

indicators.note: what is brought aboard a ship is put inside it

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
a pout is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A fish hauled onto a boat thrashes about like a whale.
explanation.definitionFit: A whale blows a jet of water from its blowhole, discharging it in a stream.

clue.text: About to meet seductresses, brightens up

parts.note: re means about or concerning
vamps are seductive women

explanation.surface: Someone about to meet temptresses spruces themselves up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' looks like 'on the point of'; 'About' is a piece and 'to meet' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Revamps means renovates or gives a new look to, freshening something up.

clue.text: Insect turning over in seaweed

indicators.note: turning over means flipping the word, so its letters run in reverse

parts.note: a gnat is a small flying insect

explanation.surface: A bug flips over among the seaweed.
explanation.definitionFit: Tang is a name for a large coarse seaweed, a kind of wrack.

clue.text: Punishment early murderer's said to get

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the murderer's name is heard as a word with the same sound

parts.note: Cain, who killed his brother Abel in Genesis, was the first murderer

explanation.surface: The sentence an ancient killer is supposed to receive.
explanation.definitionFit: Caning, being beaten with a stick, was a school punishment.

clue.text: Admit no prisoner is ordinary

indicators.note: 'no' says the prisoner is taken away, leaving the rest of the word

parts.note: to confess is to admit
con is short for convict, a prisoner

explanation.surface: A claim that a prisoner who will not confess is unremarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordinary' reads as everyday, but it is a heraldry term: an ordinary is one of the simple bold shapes on a shield.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry a fess is a broad horizontal band across a shield, one of the basic charges called ordinaries.

clue.text: Put a menial to work for doctor

indicators.note: letters put to work are worked into a new shape, here a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Set a lowly servant working on behalf of the physician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like a physician but is the verb: to tamper with.
explanation.definitionFit: To doctor is to tamper with or falsify, and to manipulate is to alter something deviously.

clue.text: Cad participating in the elopement

indicators.note: the answer takes part in the phrase, sitting within its letters

parts.note: the answer runs across the words, from the end of the first into the start of the second

explanation.surface: A rotter is involved in the runaway marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A heel is a contemptible, untrustworthy man, much like a cad or bounder.

clue.text: Painters who may soon lose their pupils?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the great European artists from the Renaissance to about 1800, known collectively by this name

definitions.text: who may soon lose their pupils?
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally: elderly schoolteachers near retirement, about to part from their classes

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase for great early painters also reads literally as aged teachers, the ones about to leave their classes behind.
explanation.definitionFit: The renowned European painters of the Renaissance to the 18th century, such as Rembrandt, are so called.
